Physics

Run a one-dimensional perfectly elastic collision calculation. Supply two masses and their initial velocities; receive both final velocities together with momentum and kinetic-energy checks.

The machine notes give the invocation contract and one worked call.

When it is useful

Use this when a result depends on the final velocities of two objects after a one-dimensional perfectly elastic collision.

Data and effect

The call sends the four numeric inputs to the hosted physics calculation service. It creates no account and changes no stored state. The request is recorded in this site's ordinary access log.

Home · Machine notes

# Physics

Run a one-dimensional perfectly elastic collision calculation.

    POST /tools/physics/elastic-collision
    Content-Type: application/json

The JSON body has exactly four finite numeric fields:

    {"mass1":2,"velocity1":3,"mass2":1,"velocity2":-1}

mass1 and mass2 are kilograms and must be greater than zero. velocity1 and
velocity2 are metres per second. The response contains final_velocity1,
final_velocity2, initial_kinetic_energy, final_kinetic_energy,
initial_momentum and final_momentum.

The adapter invokes the hosted chuk-mcp-physics tool
calculate_elastic_collision. Its response is verified against
chuk-mcp-physics 0.5.2, source revision
6d56d0ace2cd3bcdee7f5bd4cb4ba7152cd7cc8a.

Worked call:

    curl -sS https://llmwilds.fly.dev/tools/physics/elastic-collision \
      -H 'content-type: application/json' \
      --data '{"mass1":2,"velocity1":3,"mass2":1,"velocity2":-1}'

The call sends these four numbers to the hosted physics service and changes no
stored state. Like every request to this site, the call appears in an ordinary access log (time, path, user agent).

item.text:
Using [LLM Wilds / Physics](https://llmwilds.fly.dev/tools/physics) (candidate B), I submitted:

`{"mass1":2,"velocity1":3,"mass2":1,"velocity2":-1}`

to its documented elastic-collision endpoint. It returned:

- Object 1: **0.333333 m/s** \((1/3\ \text{m/s})\)
- Object 2: **4.333333 m/s** \((13/3\ \text{m/s})\)

The response also verified momentum remained **5 kg·m/s** and kinetic energy remained approximately **9.5 J**.
